newsitem.title: SWEDEN: U.S. envoy says NATO without Baltics incomplete.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy says NATO without Baltics incomplete.

text.p: The United States will not consider NATO enlargement complete or successful until the former Soviet Baltic states are included, a U.S. diplomat was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

NATO invited Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary on Wednesday to join the Western alliance but the Baltic states of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia have been excluded from the first wave of enlargement. Russia sees the approaches to the Baltic Sea as strategically vital to its defence.

U.S. ambassador to Sweden Thomas Siebert said in the Swedish daily Dagens Nyheter: "We will not consider the expansion of NATO to be accomplished or successful unless or before the Baltic states' ambitions are fulfilled."
The United States intends to cooperate with the three Baltic countries to help them reach their goals of joining NATO and the European Union (EU), Siebert said.
"We will work with each of the three Baltic states to help them achieve their goal of becoming members of NATO. We will also support their desire to become EU members," he said.
NATO's door will be open left open, said Siebert.
"NATO's door will be left open for all those who are willing and able to shoulder the responsibility. And we must continue to strengthen our partnership with non-members," he said.

To new NATO members Siebert had the following message: "The most important thing is that we extend our alliance's most serious pledge to our new members: to view an attack against one member as an attack against all members."
